governance: Non-governmental, non-profit public resource organised and operated by an international, multi-institutional group of palaeontologists (GBIF dataset description: nearly 400 contributing scientists from over 130 institutions in 24 countries). Fossil occurrences are compiled from the published literature by authorised contributors under an authorizer/enterer model and attributed to a reference (ref:N) and an enterer; taxonomic opinions are likewise referenced. Data are released under CC BY 4.0 (stated in the GBIF registration; the PBDB FAQ is a JavaScript page that could not be read by script).
versioning: The data service is versioned (1.1 retained, 1.2 is the stable production version with a published change log); the database itself is live and edited continuously, so occurrence counts (records_found, noc) are not tied to a snapshot. Taxon numbers (txn:N) and occurrence numbers (occ:N) are stable identifiers. There is no DOI for a dated snapshot of the whole database; the GBIF registration DOI 10.15468/zzoyxi identifies the dataset as a whole, not a version.
licensing: CC BY 4.0 (per the GBIF registration of the PBDB occurrence dataset).
known_issues: Every JSON response embeds an 'elapsed_time' field, so a SHA-256 recorded for an API response can never be reproduced; integrity of PBDB records has to be judged on the re-queried count, not the checksum.

The classic web pages (paleobiodb.org/classic/checkTaxonInfo?taxon_no=N, basicTaxonInfo) answer HTTP 403 to non-browser clients, so they are unusable as machine-resolvable identifiers; the equivalent data-service URL taxa/single.json?id=txn:N resolves.

Homonyms: PBDB holds animal names reused across kingdoms and phyla, e.g. Ctenophora is both the comb-jelly phylum (txn:6994) and a tipulid fly genus (txn:139744), and Tardigrada is both the water-bear phylum (txn:67137) and a disused sloth name replaced by Folivora (txn:57074). taxa/single?name= silently picks one of them, while occs/list?base_name= sums the occurrences of every taxon carrying the name without warning: on 2026-10-31 base_name=Tardigrada returned 1679 (= 1673 Folivora sloth occurrences + 6 water-bear occurrences under base_id=txn:67137) and base_name=Nautiloidea returned 2958 (= 2467 for txn:122460 + 491 for the other Nautiloidea). A count labelled with a homonymous name should be read as a count for the name, not for one taxon, unless the record queried by base_id.

Names that are nomina dubia, nomina nuda or synonyms are resolved to the accepted taxon for base_name queries (field 'tdf' documents the relation), so a count labelled with the queried name may actually be the count of the accepted taxon.

The 'noc' field of a taxon record and 'records_found' of occs/list?base_name= for the same taxon can differ by a few records (e.g. Dinosauria 37901 vs 37899 on 2026-10-31) because they are computed differently; both are legitimate PBDB numbers.
Coverage is uneven and literature-driven: many extant taxa have zero or very few occurrences, and counts for higher taxa include everything nested under them, so sums over nested taxa double-count.
Counts drift as contributors add or re-identify occurrences; a count is only reproducible to within the drift accumulated since the recorded retrieval time.
rationale: PBDB is one of the governed international infrastructures the rubric names explicitly for the 1.0 anchor: it has a peer-reviewed description of its API (Peters & McClennen 2016), a published user guide (Uhen et al. 2023), a CC BY 4.0 licence, stable taxon and occurrence identifiers, a versioned data service with a change log, and a GBIF-registered DOI. It is scored 0.9 rather than 1.0 for source authority because the database content is live and un-snapshotted (an occurrence count cannot be cited to a version) and because the DOI identifies the dataset, not a release. Independence is 0.9: occurrences are curated primary records transcribed from the published literature with no relation to this project, but PBDB is itself a compilation (occurrences and taxonomic opinions contributed by many working groups, some imported in bulk from earlier compilation projects), so independence between its constituent sources is not complete. Authenticity is 1.0: everything served is a real literature-derived record with a reference and an enterer; the fabrication risk lies in how a record cites it (wrong DOIs, homonymous names), which is scored per record.
